summary: - a) The Petitioners are wholly owned subsidiaries of the Respondent No.2, PowerGrid Corporation of India Limited, which has established project-based Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) through the Bid Process Coordinator after being successful in the bidding process. The Petitioners are engaged in a similar nature of business to that of their parent company, i.e., construction, operation and maintenance of transmission-related assets and elements including transmission lines and substations spread over various parts of the country. - c) The Scheme of amalgamation/ merger of the Transferor Companies in favour of the Transferee Company that forms the subject matter of the present Petition authority and other terms and conditions, which are not recorded here for the sake - e) The brief details of the Transferee Companies (Petitioner Nos. 12) and Transferor - f) The Petitioners have claimed that the arrangement as proposed in the Scheme is in the interest of the shareholders, creditors, and all other stakeholders of the Transferor Companies and Transferee Company, and is not prejudicial to the interests of any of the concerned shareholders, creditors, or the public at large. **3.** The Petitioners and the Respondents were heard by the Commission on 20.7.2026, 10.9.2026 and 6.11.2026 **.** The matter was admitted, and notices were issued to the Respondents to file their respective replies. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioners mainly reiterated the submissions made in the Petition. The learned counsel further submitted that the Petitioners had served the notice dated 21.05.2026 under Section 17(2) of the Act to every other licensee who transmits or distributes in the relevant areas, and the No Objection Certificate had also been received from the Respondent No.1, CTUIL, on 26.05.2026 in respect of the proposed merger. It is noted that none of the Respondents has filed its reply to the Petition. **4.** We have considered the submissions of the Petitioners. The present Petition has been filed invoking the sub-sections (1) and (3) of Section 17 of the Act **5.** The Petitioners have prayed for the approval of the Commission under subsections (1) and (3) of Section 17 of the Act. Section 17 of the Act. We have examined the scope of Section 17 of the Act, which reads as under: “Section 17 of the Electricity Act (i.e., the relevant provision in context of the present Petition) provides as follows: **7.** We have examined whether the proposed scheme of merger as submitted by the Petitioners involves a merger or transfer of their respective assets within the meaning of Section 17(1)(b) of the Act or it is the merger of the corporate identities without transfer of assets. It is necessary to examine the transaction under the proposed scheme and the manner in which such assets, rights, obligations and functions are proposed to be transferred or merged with another entity. **8.** We have perused the submission of the Petitioner with regard to the transactions under the proposed scheme. According to the Petitioner, the scheme sanction by the MCA under the provisions of Sections 230 to 233 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, after the Effective Date, but with effect from the Appointed Date, the Business Undertakings shall stand transferred to and vest in Petitioner No. 12. Transferee Company, as a going concern, together with all the respective estates, properties, assets, contracts, employees, records, approvals (including Governmental Approvals), rights, claims, title and authorities, benefits, liabilities and interest therein, subject to existing charges thereon in favour of banks and financial institutions or otherwise, as the case may be, without any further act, instrument, deed, matter or thing being made, done or executed, so as to become, as and from the Appointed Date, the estate, properties, assets, rights, claims, entitlements, title and authorities, benefits, liabilities and interest of the Transferee Company by virtue of and in the manner provided in the Scheme. Upon the Scheme becoming effective, each of the Transferor Companies shall be dissolved without being wound up, without any further act or deed. **20.** The rationale of the Scheme, as submitted by the Petitioners, is to consolidate the business for the creation of a single larger unified entity and reduce the number of entities within the group to achieve operational and management efficiencies, simplification of administrative tasks, and a simplified organisational structure. It has also been submitted that the amalgamation, pursuant to the Scheme, would inter alia, have the advantages of (i) consolidation of business, which would achieve simplification of administrative tasks, improve management efficiencies, streamline the decision making process, and at the same time maintaining the Powergrid Corporation of India Ltd’s Tariff based competitive bidding based business u/s 63 of the Act distinct from its Regulated tariff mechanism business u/s 62 of the Act; and (ii) reduction in the number of companies within the group as well as achieving reduction multiplicity of legal and regulatory compliances. It is noted that the proposed consolidation is for the ease of business operation, without affecting the tariff, nature, and operation of the transmission assets, and without affecting the interests of the stakeholders. We find that the Petitioners have complied with the requirements stipulated under the Act and TSA regarding amalgamation or merger of Petitioner No. 1 to Petitioner No. 11 with Petitioner No. 12 pursuant to the Scheme of Arrangement under Sections 230-233 of the Companies Act, 2013.
